purpose: Lowtide distant shipyard backdrop, replacing primitive far-shore geometry

outputs.prompt: Use case: background-extraction / compositing. Asset type: production game distant shipyard panorama, a transparent skyline cutout. Input image 1 is the user's desired reference, a harbor screenshot: use ONLY its detailed far-shore shipyard as the visual reference. Create a clean, very wide horizontal 3:1 panoramic asset at high resolution, ideally 3072 x 1024. Extend and reconstruct the far shore so it is complete and uninterrupted. Preserve its photorealistic North German industrial-port look: several blue-grey steel gantry cranes with substantial crossbeams, fine lattice jib cranes, corrugated maintenance sheds, dry docks, a partially built rust-red ship hull surrounded by believable scaffolding, pipework, yellow safety railings, bollards and black tire fenders on a weathered continuous concrete quay. Two large varied gantry cranes form the main central landmarks, with lower warehouse buildings at the far left and right. Sunlit weathered metal, neutral afternoon sunlight from the upper left/front, subtle blue distance haze, natural material detail and restrained contrast, consistent with the reference. Straight frontal panorama observed from across a harbor at human eye height, nearly parallel building verticals, distant compact perspective. All buildings and cranes fit inside the image with ample transparent margin above the tallest structure. The quay is a continuous horizontal opaque band along the very bottom; its bottom edge should be straight and fully opaque across the whole width so it can meet real 3D water. TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND: absolutely no sky, clouds, water, reflections, foreground ground, foreground bridge or railings, overhead foreground cables, soldiers, hands, weapons, interface, crosshair, logos, captions or watermark. Open space above and between crane arms and gantry legs must have actual clean alpha transparency, including fine lattice gaps, with no white matte fringe. Keep all shipyard details realistic and physically coherent. Output only this clean transparent environment asset.

Use case: background-extraction / compositing. Asset type: companion panoramic cutout for a game shipyard's peripheral distant shoreline. Use the input screenshot's far-shore industrial port as the photographic reference, matching its afternoon light, neutral grey-blue steel, weathered concrete and subtly hazy distance. Output a clean 3:1 wide panorama with actual transparent background, about 3000 x 1000, containing a continuous working harbor frontage: long low corrugated sheds and maintenance halls, varied small lattice cranes, pipe gantries, dock equipment, warehouse skylights, a few silos, tiny cargo containers and yellow safety rails, rust-red hull sections and dry-dock workshops. This is the lower adjoining shoreline to the left and right of a main large gantry-crane shipyard, so keep most structures low and varied and avoid large central gantry cranes or a church tower. Straight-on distant human-eye-height view across a harbor, nearly parallel verticals, no dramatic lens distortion. The industrial objects should occupy the lower half of the canvas, with generously empty transparent space above. The concrete quay and black tire fenders form an uninterrupted horizontal opaque band along the entire bottom, clean straight bottom edge. Actual transparency in every sky area and between lattice members. No sky, clouds, water, reflections, people, foreground, bridge, overhead foreground cable, weapons, game interface, crosshair, text, labels or watermark. Highly realistic material texture and physically coherent fine industrial detail.

asset_packing: Original generated RGBA preserved. RGB and alpha packed separately into 4096x1024 power-of-two atlases, with only transparent padding; every source pixel is unchanged. Native alpha-tested materials and mesh UVs meet the fully opaque quay band at the water surface.
geometry: Central reference panorama and complementary side sections at plan n=-11000, with low peripheral docks extending to e=+-88600 beyond the oblique quay views. Fixed world geometry, no gameplay collision. The harbour water continues under the whole shore. The north Fleet culvert and playable quays retain their existing geometry.
